removed: none: scheduler/market_feed_authority_process_pyintegration_test.go::TestFeedWeightSharedProcesses/AHeldAuthorityLockNeverBlocksStatus allows 1 s per status request, up from 200 ms, and holds the authority lock separately for each request
behavior: This pull request made the subtest run in parallel with the process-heavy TestFeedWeightSharedProcesses subtests, so the 200 ms bound, set when the subtests ran one after another, can fail on CPU delay alone (review https://github.com/richkuo/go-trader/pull/2097#issuecomment-7037230252). For each of /health, /status and /health, the test now takes the authority lock, starts its timer, starts a 1,500 ms release timer, sends the request, and then releases the lock. A request that waits on the lock returns only after the release, so it takes at least 1,500 ms from its own start and fails the 1 s bound wherever it is in the sequence. Each hold stays under the 2 s feedAuthorityLockWait, as before. The same three requests and the not-blocked assertion remain.

timing_source: Mutation runs (go -C scheduler test -v -count=1 -tags pyintegration -run '^TestFeedWeightSharedProcesses$/^AHeldAuthorityLockNeverBlocksStatus$' .): with handleStatus taking the authority lock, the test fails with '/status took 1.502062417s while the authority lock was held'. With /health also delayed 600 ms, one shared 1,500 ms timer and a 1 s bound pass, and the per-request hold fails with '/status took 1.50332275s'. Both mutations were reverted.
